# Command lenses: a finished command's output read as a list, offered on its
# command line. git status (its files), a compiler's errors (cc), grep -rn's
# matches; a command no lens knows gets none. @DIR@: this test's folder.
shell:cd @DIR@ && git init -q repo && cd repo && printf 'a\n' > a.txt && git add a.txt && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qm init && printf 'b\n' >> a.txt && printf 'needle here\n' > n.txt
type:cd @DIR@/repo && git status
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-lens:2 files
shell:printf 'int main(void) { return missing; }\n' > @DIR@/bad.c
type:cc -fsyntax-only @DIR@/bad.c
key:enter
wait:2.5
expect-lens:1 error
type:grep -rn needle @DIR@/repo
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-lens:1 match
type:echo plain output
key:enter
wait:1.0
expect-lens-count:3
